title: Insalata di Rinforzo
subtitle: neapolitan cauliflower salad with anchovies and olives
excerpt: Insalata di rinforzo is a Neapolitan salad traditionally made for Christmas Eve, with boiled cabbage dressed in anchovies, black and green olives, capers and red wine vinegar. It keeps and improves over several days, and is topped up with fresh ingredients as it is eaten, which is where the name rinforzo, meaning reinforcement, comes from. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Insalata di rinforzo is a fixture of Neapolitan Christmas cooking, particularly on Christmas Eve when meat is traditionally avoided. The name refers to the practice of topping up the salad as it is eaten over the festive period, reinforcing it with more olives, anchovies and pickles. It is one of the most distinctive dishes of the Campanian table.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the day before serving. It gets better as it marinates.

glossaryTerms.definition: Italian for reinforcement, referring to the tradition of topping up this Neapolitan salad with more ingredients as it is eaten over several days.
The Italian word for salad, covering both dressed vegetable salads and composed salads.

content.text: that combines boiled cabbage with anchovies, olives, capers and a sharp vinegar dressing. The key technique is blanching the cabbage until just tender, then draining it thoroughly before dressing, so the vinegar clings rather than diluting into the water left in the leaves. Serves 4.

The anchovies dissolve into the dressing as the salad rests, giving it a savoury depth that is hard to identify but easy to notice if it is missing. Make it the day before and the flavours pull together far better than when freshly dressed.

Bring a large saucepan of water to the boil. Add the cabbage pieces and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until just tender but still holding their shape. Drain well and spread on a clean towel or tray to cool and dry completely.
Once cool, transfer the cabbage to a large bowl. Add the olives, anchovies and capers.
Whisk together the red wine vinegar and olive oil. Season to taste, keeping in mind the anchovies are already salty.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss well. Cover and refrigerate for at least a few hours, or overnight. Serve at room temperature.

attrs.cause: The cabbage still had moisture in it when the dressing was added
attrs.fix: Drain the cabbage very well and leave it spread on a dry surface for at least 10 minutes before dressing

attrs.cause: The anchovies and capers both added salt without accounting for it in the dressing
attrs.fix: Do not season the dressing until you have tasted the dressed salad. Rinse the capers well and go light on any extra seasoning

attrs.symptom: Cabbage is mushy rather than tender
attrs.fix: Check at 6 minutes. It should give when pressed but still have some structure. Drain immediately and do not leave it sitting in the hot water

content.text: Insalata di rinforzo is a Neapolitan Christmas table dish, traditionally served on Christmas Eve as part of the feast of the seven fishes. It sits alongside baccalà, pasta e fagioli and fried things. The salad is replenished over the following days as it is eaten down, with more olives and anchovies added each time. By the time Christmas is over, the bowl has been through several rounds of reinforcing.
